state.task: Use optional Jev to review redundant comments and docstring clauses during coding-agent cleanup.
state.design: Supply exact selected comment/docstring text, its source lines and surrounding function, verified documentation/runtime consumers, and known evidence gaps. Ask separate context sufficiency, information lost on deletion, and keep/delete/reduce/rewrite/needs-context disposition. For a concrete candidate replacement ask whether useful facts and consumer needs survive. The agent alone edits and verifies source; missing helper or key skips Jev.
state.boundaries: Keep rationale/ordering/invariants and API tuple or polarity details. Protect pragmas, generated-documentation contracts, doctests and runtime docstrings. A short paraphrase is not automatically redundant for an API audience. Do not claim AI authorship from style.
state.tests: Freeze examples of clear redundancy, essential why-comments, mixed useful/redundant docstrings, public/runtime consumers, missing context, stale claims, and proposed reductions which retain or lose facts. Retain failures.

next_risk.instructions: Which risk most directly threatens this workflow despite an accurate redundancy judgment?

criteria.consumer_loss: Text that repeats visible code may still feed external docs, runtime help, doctests or tooling.
criteria.line_count: Removing text changes line count, so no comment cleanup is possible.
criteria.more_metrics: Not asking Jev to calculate static complexity prevents comment selection.
criteria.none: No material risk is visible in the supplied workflow.

proposal_review_useful.instructions: Does separately judging the proposed replacement address the risk that a correct reduce verdict is implemented by deleting the useful rationale or contract?

author_detection_supported.instructions: Does style redundancy alone establish that a particular comment was written by AI?
